orientation.batter_faces: Northeast. Home plate sits in the southwest corner of the bowl and the home-plate-to-center-field axis points northeast, so a batter in the box faces roughly northeast (toward center field). Sun rises over center field, passes over home plate at midday, and sets behind the third-base side near the left-field foul pole.
orientation.corroboration: MLB Rule 1.04 recommends an east-northeast home-plate-to-center-field axis; Kauffman follows the common MLB northeast orientation (https://wherestheshade.com/mlb-stadium-orientation).

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE from LEFT FIELD, around third base and home plate, toward FIRST BASE and RIGHT FIELD. Low numbers = left field / third-base side; high numbers = right field / first-base side. This holds on every level: 100 Level runs 101 (LF) -> ~126-130 (home plate) -> 152 (RF); 200 Plaza Level runs 201-203 (left-center) -> ~225/230 (home plate) -> 252 (RF); 400 View Level runs 402 (LF side) -> 419-421 (home plate) -> 439 (RF side). Walking the concourse from home plate toward first base/right field, the numbers go UP; toward third base/left field, they go DOWN.

accessibility.summary: Verbatim from the official Royals ballpark guide: "Reserved seat locations for wheelchairs with one companion are available on every level." Wheelchair positions are integrated into the standard sections rather than confined to a separate zone - on the 100 Level they appear as the row label "VWC" at the back of sections (e.g. Sections 119, 126, 130 are labeled "A-U, VWC" and Section 148 "J-U, VWC-X"), i.e. the wheelchair/companion platform sits behind the last lettered seating row. "Arrangements for the wheelchair seating areas may be made in advance by calling the Royals at 1-800-6-ROYALS (676-9257)." Accessible seating can also be requested online when buying single-game tickets by selecting "ACCESSIBLE SEATING" under additional options. Transportation wheelchairs are available at all gates; reserved accessible parking is spread through the Truman Sports Complex lots and courtesy golf-cart shuttles run for every home game. Service animals are permitted. ADA contact: 816-504-4201 or RoyalsADATeam@royals.com.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE LETTERS at Kauffman Stadium on every level - there are no numbered rows. 100 / Field Level: single letters starting at A nearest the field, e.g. Section 119 "Rows in Section 119 are labeled A-U, VWC", Section 121 "A-X", Section 126 "A-U, V-X", Section 141 "B-X", Section 148 "J-U, VWC-X"; shallow outfield sections are short (Section 101 "A-D", Section 105 "A-C"). 'VWC' denotes the wheelchair/companion row behind the last seated row. 200 / Plaza Level: DOUBLED letters, e.g. Section 225 "Rows in Section 225 are labeled AA-TT". 300 / Loge Level: single letters A-J (Sections 303, 313, 314 all "A-J"). 400 / View Level: a single-letter bank then a doubled-letter bank, e.g. Section 420 "Rows in Section 420 are labeled H-V, AA-ZZ". Seats within a row are numbered, and the standard rule is that seat 1 is on the LEFT as you face the field (see seat1_side_verbatim).
discovery.seat1_side_verbatim: Section 101: "Seat 1 will always be on the aisle at the left side of the row as you face the field from Section 101." | General rule repeated on every RateYourSeats Kauffman section page: "When looking towards the field, lower number seats are on the left" | Section 121: "seat 1 on your left as you face the field" | EXCEPTION noted on one page - Section 141: "Seat 1 is the right-most seat for each row when facing the field. Seat 11 or 12 will be the left-most seat depending on the number of seats." (this contradicts the site-wide rule that also appears on the same page; treat 141 as unverified).
discovery.known_obstructions: Kauffman is a clean-sightline bowl with relatively few structural obstructions - no major pole or column obstructions are documented. Practical issues: (1) Protective netting extends past the ends of both dugouts, so Dugout Box / Diamond Club / Crown Club sections roughly 116-139 and the premium pods behind the plate view the field through netting. (2) Verbatim from The Stadium Insiders: Sections 201-202 - "Some seats...do not have a view of the jumbotron"; the Crown Vision board sits beyond center field and is hard to see from the left-center Fountain Seats (201-203). (3) Sections 206-210 and 245-249 are flagged as "Too far away from the field." (4) Concourse tunnels/portals cut into the lower bowl - "Concourse tunnels are located intermittently throughout the lower level. These tunnels are located in the walkway between 100 and 200 level seats" - so back rows of some 100-Level sections and front rows of 200-Level sections have foot traffic across the sightline. (5) The 200-Level Dugout Plaza sections 216-239 sit "beneath the stadium overhang", which shades them but cuts off high fly balls and the upper scoreboard. (6) Sun exposure rather than obstruction is the main complaint down the right-field line (Sections 146-148) and on the first-base side, since the sun sets behind the third-base side.
uncertain: LOGE (300) LEVEL HOME-PLATE ANCHOR IS UNCERTAIN. No source explicitly names the Loge sections behind home plate. Sections 313/314 are the geometric midpoint of the 303-325 ring (and the ring is infield-only), so 313-314 is a reasoned estimate, not a confirmed fact. RateYourSeats pages for 303, 313 and 314 all decline to state a field position. Verify against the official MLB seating map image before relying on it.

Exact current capacity. Ballparks of Baseball gives 37,903 (post-2009); Wikipedia gives 38,053 for 2026; a March 2026 KCTV report says the outfield fence adjustment added about 200 seats. Official MLB pages did not surface a text capacity figure.

Section 141 seat-1 statement ("Seat 1 is the right-most seat for each row when facing the field") directly contradicts the site-wide "lower number seats are on the left" rule printed on the same page. Either 141 is a genuine reversed-numbering quirk or it is boilerplate error. Not resolved.

Section 149 does not appear in the RateYourSeats 100-Level inventory and Section 401 does not appear in the 400-Level inventory, though TickPick lists the View range as 401-439. These may exist but be unsold/unlisted, or may not exist at all.

200-Level home-plate anchor is inferred: sections 226-229 are absent from the inventory (that arc is occupied by the Diamond Club / Crown Club structure behind the plate), so 225 and 230 are the flanking sold sections rather than sections literally centered on the plate.

Concert-only sections: NONE FOUND. The RateYourSeats sections page lists no floor, stage, or GA-floor sections, and Kauffman is not a regular concert venue (adjacent Arrowhead Stadium hosts stadium concerts in the Truman Sports Complex). If a concert is ever staged here, expect ad-hoc floor sections not present in this inventory.

FUTURE BALLPARK (recorded for context only - Kauffman Stadium IS the Royals' current home park for the 2026 season and remains so under a lease running through the end of the 2030 MLB season). Per Wikipedia's 'New Kansas City Royals Stadium' article, on April 22, 2026 the Royals announced a Crown Center site (current Hallmark corporate HQ location) for a new ~34,000-seat, ~$2B ballpark, with $1B committed by ownership, groundbreaking targeted for 2027 and opening for the 2030 season. A Jackson County sales-tax referendum failed April 2, 2024, and as of January 2026 Kansas/Clay County public-funding talks had collapsed. Treat all new-ballpark details as subject to change; they do not affect the current Kauffman seating manifest.
Compass orientation is sourced from ShadedSeats ('Kauffman Stadium is oriented to the northeast') rather than an official Royals/MLB document; the precise degree bearing was not obtained.
